title: The Unofficial Homecoming
premise: Theo Underhill, the debate team captain whose careful silence keeps his fractured household from shattering, inherits his late grandmother's recipe box and finds index cards that are not recipes at all — they're coded records of what the school board buried decades ago: a fire, a cover-up, and students who were made to disappear. Following the cards pulls Theo into an unlikely crew of misfits who become the family he never had at home, even as the board's remaining insiders close ranks. When the last card reveals his own family's complicity, Theo must choose between the careful boy he's been and the truth-teller his grandmother believed he could be — and he wins the argument that matters by refusing to debate it at all, reading her testimony aloud at the homecoming assembly.
about_author: August Kavanagh is a former high school debate coach who spent six years listening to teenagers say true things in formal language. They write young adult fiction about kids who are braver than the adults around them, and they still keep their grandmother's recipe box on the kitchen counter.

chapters.title: The Careful Boy
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. We meet him mid-debate tournament, flawless on stage, then watch him shrink the moment he gets home, where his father's rules and his mother's exhaustion demand silence. He wins every argument except the ones that count. Emotional beat: the ache of being excellent everywhere except where you live.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ash
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. After Grandma Ruth's funeral, Theo is tasked with clearing her kitchen and finds the recipe box — but interleaved with the cards for lemon bars are index cards written in shorthand, dated across forty years, referencing names he doesn't know and one word repeated: HOLLOWAY. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by mystery.

chapters.title: Decoding Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He tests the first card like a recipe and realizes the 'ingredients' are directions — measurements map to dates, temperatures to room numbers in the old wing of Marsh Creek High. His best friend Priya catches him obsessing and refuses to be left out. Emotional beat: the first spark of shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Old Wing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The two sneak into the sealed 1970s wing during homecoming setup and find the card's coordinates lead to a bricked-over doorway behind the auditorium. Someone has scratched a tally of eleven marks into the brick. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the library archive, they match the tally to a 1974 fire report listing zero casualties — yet Grandma Ruth's cards name eleven students who were 'relocated' afterward. One name stops Theo cold: Underhill. Emotional beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Dinner Without Answers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo probes his father at dinner using debate tactics and watches him deflect with practiced ease — too practiced. His mother leaves the table mid-meal. That night Theo finds his father burning papers in the grill. Emotional beat: suspicion turning toward home.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. To decode faster, they recruit Marcus (yearbook nerd), Dez (lock-picking theater kid), and Sam (journalism editor whose paper got shuttered by the board). Eating takeout in the newspaper room, Theo feels something unfamiliar: a table where he isn't performing. Emotional beat: found family begins.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. The crew confirms the fire was arson-cover for hazing gone fatal, and the board traded silence for funding from the victims' families' employer. Grandma Ruth, then a cafeteria worker, documented everything. Emotional beat: righteous anger with no legal outlet.

chapters.title: A Warning in Lemon Bars
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A tin of lemon bars appears on Theo's porch with a note in his grandmother's handwriting style: STOP STIRRING. But Ruth is dead — someone is forging her hand. Theo realizes the box was never lost; it was hidden from someone still alive. Emotional beat: being watched.

chapters.title: Vice Principal Voss
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The trail leads to Vice Principal Voss, whose signature appears on the relocation paperwork — and whose office displays a photo of a young board chairman: Theo's grandfather. Priya urges Theo to slow down; he can't. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by truth.

chapters.title: Homecoming Week
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Amid pep rallies and float-building, the crew works in plain sight, and Marcus documents everything. Theo is nominated to speak at the assembly as debate champion — a platform handed to him by the very people he's investigating. Emotional beat: irony sharpening into opportunity.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A new card surfaces in the box that Ruth could not have written — it describes Theo's search, present tense. The forger is inside the house. Theo sets a trap with a false card and waits up all night. Emotional beat: paranoia in your own kitchen.

chapters.title: His Father's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The trap works: his father takes the bait card. Confronted, Dad confesses he's been paying Voss for years to keep the box buried — Grandfather Underhill helped orchestrate the cover-up, and the family name depends on it staying buried. Emotional beat: the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Runaway Cards
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The box vanishes from Theo's locker; Dez tracks it to Voss's office and photographs the theft, but gets caught and suspended on fabricated grounds. The crew realizes the board will destroy them one by one. Emotional beat: fear, and choosing each other anyway.

chapters.title: Ruth's Last Card
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya deciphers the final card Ruth wrote before her death: not evidence, but a letter — 'to whoever finally stirs.' Ruth knew she was running out of time and left the ending deliberately unfinished, trusting a child to finish it. Emotional beat: inheritance as love.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Name
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cross-referencing yearbooks, they find the eleventh relocated student didn't die or move — she grew up to be Theo's mother, who changed her name after the fire. His mother has known everything and stayed silent to protect him. Emotional beat: compassion replacing betrayal.

chapters.title: Mother and Son
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Mother and son finally speak honestly. She gives him the one document Ruth entrusted to her — the original coroner's letter — and admits she was waiting for Theo to be ready, not permission-giving but faith-keeping. Emotional beat: the argument at home ends in alliance.

chapters.title: Quorum
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. With the suspension hearing looming, the crew goes public: Sam's resurrected underground paper drops the story, families of the eleven come forward, and the board calls an emergency session — scheduled, cynically, right before the homecoming assembly. Emotional beat: momentum against machinery.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the board session, Theo does what he does best — argues — but Voss produces the forged 'STOP STIRRING' note to paint Ruth as unstable and Theo as a grieving kid chasing ghosts. The board votes to seal the records permanently. Emotional beat: defeat that clarifies.

chapters.title: What Debating Is For
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Theo nearly quits; Priya reframes it — he's been winning arguments his whole life, but Ruth didn't leave him an argument, she left him testimony. You don't debate testimony. You deliver it. The crew plans the assembly takeover. Emotional beat: strategy born of heart.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the assembly, when called to give his speech, Theo sets down his prepared remarks and reads Ruth's cards aloud, name by name, while Marcus projects the archives and the eleven families stand one by one. Voss resigns on the spot; the board's vote collapses under witnesses. Emotional beat: catharsis — the careful boy, uncareful at last.

chapters.title: Stirring
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, weeks later. The old wing reopens as a memorial; Dez is reinstated; the school paper prints again. At home, Theo cooks one of Ruth's actual recipes with both parents — awkwardly, together. The last line of her final card, now finished in his handwriting: 'Serves everyone.' Emotional beat: belonging, earned and shared.
